subject: Sync: midterm uplift and co-term alignment for Solstice Health
messages:
From: Emily Zhang <emily.z@solsticehealth.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-25T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Mid-cycle capacity growth — options for top-up and co-term?

Hi Marcus / Lauren,

Quick note from our end — we saw a sharp uptick in inference volume over the past 6 weeks after onboarding two new pilot customers. Our current Dedicated pool is at ~145% of committed capacity and trending higher. Procurement asked we surface options for: (a) adding capacity mid-contract, (b) annualizing / co-terming so usage aligns with our fiscal year, and (c) any short-term bridge credits while we finalize forecast.

Attached is a very small usage snapshot (Solstice_usage_snapshot_Apr2027.csv) and the plan we reviewed with your solutions team (Solstice_MA_plan_v2.pdf). High-level asks:
- Can Redwood provide a fast top-up path for +30% capacity that doesn’t require a full contract renegotiation?
- If we do an annualize / co-term to Dec 31, what discounting/credit mechanics are typical?
- Any possibility of a short bridge voucher or temporary burst band while forecasting is finalized?

We’re hoping to avoid a multi-week procurement loop if possible. Happy to take a 30-minute sync.

Thanks,
Emily
Head of Cloud Ops
Solstice Health

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Emily Zhang <emily.z@solsticehealth.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-25T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Mid-cycle capacity growth — options for top-up and co-term?

Emily — appreciate the heads up and the attachments. Short answers below, then a suggested next step.

Option A — Immediate top-up (fast path)
- We can provision a +30% dedicated capacity in 3–5 business days for a short-term top-up. Billing options: pro-rata invoice for the remainder of the current billing period OR staged monthly top-up to spread cost across the remaining term.
- No re-signing of the main MSA required for a top-up amendment; we use a one-page Capacity Addendum.

Option B — Annualize / co-term (longer path)
- If you want to annualize and co-term to 2027-12-31, typical treatments are: annualized add-on (convert extra monthly usage into committed capacity with an annual invoice) or a voucher that bridges monthly overage into credit toward a new annual commit.
- Typical commercial levers: 5–10% tactical discount if you move to an annualized commit, with the exact % tied to committed GPU-hours and a 12–18 month commit.

Option C — Bridge voucher / burst credit
- We can offer a limited voucher (one-off credit) to cover overage for up to 60 days while you finalize forecasts. Voucher requires sign-off from finance/RevOps — I can put forward a request.

Questions I have from your attachments / to validate pricing:
- Can you confirm the run-rate (GPU-hours/day) you expect for the next 3 months?
- Are the two new pilots expected to convert to paid this quarter?

Suggested next step: 30-minute call tomorrow to align on volume. If you’re comfortable, I’ll draft two quick straw quotes: (1) +30% top-up (staged billing) and (2) +30% annualized with a proposed % discount and payment terms.

If helpful I’ll include Ben from Pricing for final discount approval.

—Marcus
Senior Account Exec | Redwood Inference

Ben — forwarding Emily’s ask (see attached). Marcus and I discussed internally. Key negotiation posture I recommend: move fast on an option that prevents service disruption and avoid heavy discounting. Proposed commercial options (internal only):

1) Staged Top-up — +30% capacity (3–5 day provision)
  - Billing: monthly staged invoices for remainder of term
  - Discount: 0% base (we could offer a small operational credit instead, e.g., one month service credit)
  - Contract: Capacity Addendum (minimal legal)

2) Annualize with co-term to 2027-12-31
  - Billing: annual invoice for the new committed amount
  - Discount: up to 8% (tiered by commit size) if they annualize and prepay 6–12 months; 5% if billed net-30
  - Note: requires procurement lead time (DocuSign + amendment) — ask Emily whether procurement can move quickly

3) Bridge voucher (short-term)
  - Credit to offset overage while forecast locks (valid for 60 days)
  - Requires RevOps sign-off and one-off approval — helpful when procurement needs more time

Action for Ben: can you confirm whether we have headroom to approve an 8% tactical discount for this account (SOL-2027-23871)? Also, please confirm capacity availability in us-west for a +30% pool — Marcus flagged potential scheduling constraints for that region.

Thanks,
Lauren
Director, Sales Operations | Redwood Inference

Marcus / Lauren / Ben — thanks for the quick turnaround and options. We discussed internally with procurement and finance.

Decision summary:
- We’d like to take Option 1 (Staged Top-up) to avoid service disruption and get the +30% on the platform immediately. Please proceed with provisioning in us-west.
- For commercial treatment we prefer staged monthly billing for the remainder of the term (no prepay) plus a single bridge credit to offset April overage (we estimate ~$12k).
- Procurement asks that any Capacity Addendum reference our Master Subscription Agreement and be processed via DocuSign with standard Solstice payment terms (Net‑60).

Could you (a) send a short quote reflecting the staged top-up and the one-off bridge credit and (b) confirm provisioning ETA once signed? If necessary we can approve a minimal one-page addendum quickly.

Thanks — cc’ing Emily to keep her in the loop.

Carlos R.
